issues.legal_issue: A killing in a sudden fight is excluded from murder when it occurs without premeditation, in the heat of passion upon a sudden quarrel, and without the offender taking undue advantage or acting cruelly or unusually.
material_facts: The fatal injury was inflicted during a sudden and free fight, without premeditation and in the heat of passion following a sudden quarrel.
Both contending parties were armed with dangerous sharp-edged weapons.
The deceased’s party was not unarmed or armed only with weapons that were not lethal or dangerous.
issues.conclusion: The facts fell within Exception 4 to Section 300 of the Indian Penal Code, so the appellant could not be convicted of murder under Section 302; the offence was reduced to culpable homicide not amounting to murder under Section 304.
issues.legal_principle: Exception 4 to Section 300 of the Indian Penal Code applies when a death is caused without premeditation in a sudden fight, in the heat of passion upon a sudden quarrel, and without the offender taking undue advantage or acting in a cruel or unusual manner. Whether conduct was cruel or unusual depends on the circumstances; where both sides in a free fight are armed with dangerous weapons, the use of such weapons does not, in those circumstances, establish that either side acted cruelly or unusually. The court relied on no earlier cases.

issues.definition: When a murder conviction arises from a sudden fight without premeditation, in the heat of passion after a sudden quarrel, and without undue advantage or cruel or unusual conduct, the conviction is reduced to culpable homicide not amounting to murder if both sides were armed with dangerous weapons.

issues.legal_issue: When culpable homicide not amounting to murder is committed with the intention to cause death or bodily injury likely to cause death, the offence falls under Part I rather than Part II of Section 304 of the Indian Penal Code.
material_facts: The fatal injury was inflicted with the intention to cause death or bodily injury likely to cause death.
The offence was reduced from murder to culpable homicide not amounting to murder.
issues.conclusion: The offence fell under Part I of Section 304 of the Indian Penal Code.
issues.legal_principle: Section 304, Part I, of the Indian Penal Code applies where culpable homicide not amounting to murder is committed with the intention of causing death or bodily injury likely to cause death. The court relied on no earlier cases.

predicates.culpable_homicide_case: The case concerns culpable homicide not amounting to murder.
predicates.intention_to_cause_death_or_likely_fatal: The offender intended to cause death or bodily injury likely to cause death.

issues.definition: In a culpable homicide case, an intention to cause death or likely fatal injury means the offence falls under Part I.

issues.legal_issue: An appellate court may determine the legal character of an offence from proved facts even when the specific legal point was not clearly raised in the courts below.
material_facts: The lower courts’ findings established the circumstances of the fatal injury and the nature of the fight.
The applicability of the sudden-fight exception had not been clearly raised in the High Court.
Determining the offence from the established facts was a question of law.
issues.conclusion: The court was not precluded from deciding the exact nature of the offence on the basis of the findings, although the point had not been clearly raised below.
issues.legal_principle: Where the question is the legal nature of an offence deducible from proved facts, it is a question of law, and an appellate court may decide it by examining the findings even if the point was not clearly elucidated in the courts below. The court relied on no earlier cases.
